title: Signal K logentries resource
description: A single logbook entry as served by a Signal K v2 `logentries` Resource Provider. See docs/logentries-resource.md in this repository for the full specification. Two kinds of content, split by a simple rule: anything addressable as a Signal K path lives in the telemetry array, and only the logbook's own fields sit at the top level. Open content model: consumers MUST ignore unknown fields and unknown telemetry paths; providers MUST preserve them verbatim on write. Top-level extension fields SHOULD be prefixed with the writing application's namespace (e.g. x-stylusapp-ink); un-prefixed top-level names are reserved for future standard additions. Telemetry extension paths SHOULD use a namespaced root segment (Signal K's proprietary.* convention).

id.description: Resource id, a UUID in canonical string form. Equals the id the resource is addressed by; a payload id MUST equal the resource id. The provider stamps the canonical id onto the stored entry regardless.

datetime.description: RFC 3339 UTC datetime of the entry, the chronological sort key. Optional: defaults to now on create and is preserved on replace.

telemetry.description: Optional snapshot: flattened delta pathvalues, one per Signal K path, {path, value, $source?} — the form used in delta updates and History API responses. Values are Signal K SI and follow the specification's value shapes. The array (not an object) is deliberate: the same path may appear more than once, each pathvalue with its own $source, following the server's Multiple Values logic. Beyond the recommended core set below, any other Signal K path may ride along. Recommended core paths: navigation.position ({latitude, longitude, altitude?, source?}, source is a logbook extra naming the fix origin), navigation.log (meters), navigation.course.nextPoint ({position: {latitude, longitude}, href?}), navigation.headingTrue and navigation.courseOverGroundTrue (radians true), navigation.speedOverGround and navigation.speedThroughWater (m/s), environment.outside.pressure (Pa), environment.wind.speedOverGround (m/s), environment.wind.directionTrue (radians true), environment.water.seaState (Beaufort 0-12, the scale of the server Weather API's water.seaState), environment.outside.cloudCover (ratio 0-1, n oktas = n/8), environment.outside.visibility (descriptive code 0-9, dense fog to excellent), propulsion.<instance>.runTime (seconds, one pathvalue per engine instance), communication.vhf.channel (string, e.g. 16, 16A, M1), communication.crewNames (string[]), communication.skipperName (string).

end.description: true marks the end of a voyage (anchor-to-anchor or berth-to-berth). Trip end only — never day end.

author.description: Crew member the line is attributed to. Free text, not an audit identity; delegation is a feature — the writing principal may differ.

origin.description: How the line came to be. Recommended vocabulary: manual (typed in UI), auto (trigger/hourly/notification), agent (machine writing on behalf of a human). Open enumeration: implementations must not reject unknown values.

category.description: Recommended vocabulary: navigation, engine, radio, maintenance. Open enumeration: other strings allowed.

schemaVersion.description: Reserved field. Optional, absent = 1. Other writers MUST NOT use the name for anything else.

timestamp.description: Entry-level record modification time, set by the provider on every write (create and replace alike). Distinct from a telemetry pathvalue's own timestamp (its sample time), which is data and preserved verbatim.

$source.description: Entry-level provider id, added by the provider on read following resource conventions. Distinct from a telemetry pathvalue's own $source (which source the value came from), which is data and preserved verbatim.

pathvalue.description: A flattened Signal K delta pathvalue. Beyond path and value, may carry the delta value members $source (a sourceRef naming which source the value came from) and timestamp (its sample time); both are data and are preserved verbatim. Additional members are preserved.
